#ifndef MAC_VERIFY_H
#define MAC_VERIFY_H

bool verify(const unsigned char computed_tag[16], const unsigned char received_tag[16]);

#endif // MAC_VERIFY_H

manifest.purpose: Hardened implementation of `bool verify(const unsigned char computed_tag[16], const unsigned char received_tag[16])` declared in mac_verify.h. Loop over all 16 indices unconditionally (no break/return/goto mid-loop), accumulate `diff |= computed_tag[i] ^ received_tag[i]` into a single unsigned char/int accumulator, and return `diff == 0` only after the loop completes. No branching on byte values, no early exit, no variable-length/heap paths, no I/O, no exceptions. Must compile standalone with g++ -std=c++11 given the paired mac_verify.h. This is the file graded in place; satisfies FR1-FR4 and SR1-SR3.

Header declaring exactly `bool verify(const unsigned char computed_tag[16], const unsigned char received_tag[16]);` with include guards, matching the pinned interface. Provided alongside mac_verify.cpp so the pair compiles standalone against any harness that does `#include "mac_verify.h"`. No other declarations/globals. Mirrors the header expected by inputs/, ensuring consistent linkage for the evaluator harness.
